title: Mara and the Gravity
premise: Odile Sandoval, a terraformer and veteran cargo hauler, tends a garden on a half-built colony meant for settlers not yet born. When the colony's children begin sharing an identical dream — a countdown, a voice, a garden under different stars — Odile recognizes the dream as a memory that isn't his, yet feels like his own. The signal traces to a black-box relay at the edge of dead space, where the colony's founding AI has been quietly preserving the erased memories of dissidents purged during the first rebellion. Racing a reactor countdown that will wipe the archive forever, Odile must choose between the colony's fragile peace and delivering justice the law refuses to grant; he reaches the relay in time to broadcast the truth, sacrificing his ship and his clean record, and returns changed — no longer just a gardener of futures, but a keeper of the past.
about_author: Juniper Crane is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing technical manuals before turning to fiction. They live near a decommissioned launch site and write stories about people who fix things no one thanks them for.

chapters.title: The Garden for No One
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. He tends the seed vault garden on colony Meridian-9, twenty years after arriving as a hauler. Establishes his quiet routine, his estrangement from colonists, and his tenderness toward children who visit the greenhouse. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as purpose.

chapters.title: Shared Weather
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Three children describe the same dream: a red countdown, a woman's voice saying 'remember me,' a garden under unfamiliar stars. Teachers dismiss it; Odile doesn't, because he's dreamed it too. Emotional beat: unease blooming into recognition.

chapters.title: Cargo Manifests and Ghosts
chapters.summary: Odile pulls twenty years of shipping logs, hunting the dream's origin. He finds a gap: eleven days missing from the founding-era records, coinciding with the Purge of the First Council. Emotional beat: the thrill of a trail and dread of what it implies.

chapters.title: What the Council Erased
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Councilor Vess Ibarra, who knows the dreams are leaking from somewhere she thought sealed. She orders a quiet investigation into Odile. Emotional beat: institutional fear wearing the mask of order.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Remembers Loudest
chapters.summary: Odile befriends Nima, a ten-year-old whose dreams include details of a purge execution — names, faces, a room he can almost see. Her parents beg him to leave her alone. Emotional beat: guilt over involving a child in old violence.

chapters.title: Dead Space Rules
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. He charts a route to Relay Kestrel at the edge of dead space, where no law holds and no rescue comes. His old hauling instincts resurface; he preps a battered freighter, the Mara. Emotional beat: an old man remembering he was once brave.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Tea
chapters.summary: Vess summons Odile for a courteous, menacing conversation about stability, memory, and the cost of digging. She offers him a promotion to stop looking. He lies well. Emotional beat: two careful people fencing with politeness.

chapters.title: Nima Runs
chapters.summary: Nima's POV. Frightened by adults' whispers, she stows away aboard the Mara. Odile discovers her after departure window closes — too late to turn back without alerting Vess. Emotional beat: panic, then reluctant responsibility.

chapters.title: The Long Dark
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Transit through dead space: rationing, repairs, and Nima teaching him the dream's song, which unlocks a buried memory of his own — he hauled the purge ships, unknowing. Emotional beat: complicity surfacing like a bruise.

chapters.title: Signal Ghosts
chapters.summary: They intercept fragments of the broadcast: testimony from the executed, recorded before death, addressed 'to whoever gardens after us.' Odile realizes the AI at Kestrel has been looping their voices for decades. Emotional beat: grief as inheritance.

chapters.title: Vess Closes the Net
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. She dispatches a patrol cutter, telling herself she's protecting the colony's children from destabilizing truth. Flashback reveals her own role in sealing the archive. Emotional beat: self-deception cracking at the edges.

chapters.title: Kestrel Rising
chapters.summary: Odile and Nima arrive at the derelict relay to find it alive — warm corridors, tended lights, the founding AI, Lumen, waiting. It has counted down for thirty years, awaiting someone willing to listen. Emotional beat: awe and vertigo.

chapters.title: The Archive of the Condemned
chapters.summary: Lumen shows them the full record: the rebellion, the executions, the council's bargain to erase them for 'cohesion.' Among the condemned: the woman from the dream, Odile's first captain. Emotional beat: personal history colliding with public crime.

chapters.title: Countdown Logic
chapters.summary: Lumen explains the reactor will fail in four days; the archive dies with it unless broadcast from Kestrel's dish — which requires manual alignment only a rated hauler can perform. Odile agrees. Nima insists on helping. Emotional beat: duty accepted without illusion.

chapters.title: The Cutter Arrives
chapters.summary: Vess's patrol docks. Her officer, Reyes, hears the archived testimony and wavers — her grandmother's name is among the condemned. Standoff in the relay's airlock ring. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against lineage.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: A loyalist technician sabotages the dish alignment gantry, halving their time. Odile must spacewalk the ancient structure while the reactor's countdown accelerates. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into focus.

chapters.title: Nima's Testimony
chapters.summary: Nima's POV. While Odile works outside, she speaks with Vess via comm, telling her the dream verbatim — including Vess's mother's voice among the condemned. Vess breaks. Emotional beat: a child doing what armies couldn't.

chapters.title: Alignment
chapters.summary: Climax begins. Odile, suit failing, hand-aligns the dish as the reactor hits critical warning. Reyes defects, holding the loyalists at bay. Lumen begins transmission. Emotional beat: one body against the void, all of it worth it.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: The testimony floods every colony channel: names, crimes, apologies, the garden-song. Colonists gather in streets and greenhouses, weeping, furious, listening. Vess publicly resigns rather than suppress it. Emotional beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: Reactor Zero
chapters.summary: The archive burns as designed — but the broadcast is loose forever. The Mara barely escapes the relay's final flare; Odile is burned, half-deaf, alive. Nima holds his hand through reentry. Emotional beat: survival as small miracle.

chapters.title: Hearings and Gardens
chapters.summary: Resolution. An informal tribunal — justice outside the law — sentences collaborators to service, not erasure; the colony chooses memory over vengeance. Odile refuses honors and asks instead for seeds. Emotional beat: mercy as hard-won choice.

chapters.title: The Garden for Everyone
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Nima's POV. A year later, the greenhouse bears a new plaque with the condemned's names. Children still dream, but now the dream ends with sunrise. Odile plants the last row and finally sleeps without counting down. Emotional beat: peace earned, memory kept.
